title: Eyleme NeedSpec development request
description: Defines a human need, acceptance criteria and development boundaries for Eyleme. Schema validity does not establish authorization, model availability, repository access or satisfied acceptance criteria.

request_id.description: Stable request identifier. Uniqueness is enforced by the controller.

revision.description: Revision of the same request. Monotonic progression is enforced by the protocol.

repository.description: Identifier of the source repository; not evidence of access or ownership.

objective.description: The concrete outcome expected by the contributor.

id.description: Criterion identifier within the request. Identifier uniqueness is checked separately.

scenario.description: Initial conditions and the user action or event.

expected.description: An observable and verifiable expected outcome.

allowed_paths.description: Allowed paths or patterns relative to the target repository. Pattern semantics, normalization, symbolic links and actual write boundaries are enforced separately.

dependency_policy.description: First-party Rust production policy. The dependency inventory is checked separately; explicitly approved development and training tools have a separate inventory.

targets.description: Target environment identifiers. Support and actual execution evidence are checked separately.

authorization_ref.description: Opaque reference to a trusted authorization record. Its presence or contents grant no permission; identity, scope and validity are verified separately.

budget.description: Upper bounds for this request. Counters, stopping behavior and any narrower deployment budget are enforced at execution.

publish_target.description: Requested delivery type; it grants neither publication permission nor merge authority.

repo_identifier.description: Target repository. Its relationship to the source repository and access authorization are verified separately.

roles.description: Optional role assignments. These are configuration references, not claims that models are available; deployment configuration resolves them.
